_comment: Scenario-staged rout-then-ANNIHILATION demo: a lone low-morale (1) player infantry block of 12 is charged head-on by two 12-horse cavalry troops and BREAKS -- it enters routing (drawn faded) and flees. The squadrons are shallow and spawn close so their facing-front is in spatha reach at regiment contact. Routing units are still valid combat targets, and the cavalry (8.5 m/s sprint) are faster than the fleeing infantry (4.0 m/s sprint, 1.3 x that in flight), so pursuit is relentless: each routed man runs on his own from the riders he sees toward his own back edge (SoldierFlightStep), the runners scatter, and each rider rides at the runner nearest him and cuts him down on the move (SoldierPursuitStep; at Cannae the Numidian horse pursued the fleeing Roman cavalry and cut most of them down, Polybius 3.116). The casualties keep its morale from recovering, so it never rallies and is ANNIHILATED (soldiers reach zero) rather than escaping or rallying. The scene runs on a custom tall map (field 1600x2400, flat) with every actor staged in the deep south, so the flight has room; a second, safe player unit (140 Spearmen) stays in the fight so the battle doesn't declare defeat the instant the infantry routs. Measured with dense 2-tick FULL dumps on seeds 0 to 4, 2026-11-20 on #1949's branch: it routs at tick 60 and is still routing at tick 200 (pinned) with 5 to 10 of its 12 men left; the lead squadron (uid 3) is after it (target_enemy_uid 0) inside ticks 200 to 300 on every seed (pinned); and the last runner falls at tick 350 on the clip's own seed (seed 0), 386 on seeds 1, 2 and 4, and 242 on seed 3 (absent inside ticks 250 to 1200, pinned). The routing pin was at tick 250, which seed 3, cut down by tick 242, no longer reaches. On main c36560fa it was caught at tick 420, fought on the move to tick 542 and cut down between ticks 648 and 650. The pins were: ROUTING at tick 540, uid 3 targeting it and engaged in melee inside ticks 480 to 600, and gone inside ticks 610 to 700. The bottom-up flight and the riders' own pursuit (#1949) run it down earlier on four seeds and about as late on one, so the windows move to cover every seed, and the engaged pin is retired: riders who cut runners down on the move are not a block engaged in melee. Camera frames the clash and then pans with the chase (website/tools/demo-catalog.sh records 360 frames at 30 fps, to tick 720, which shows the kill on every seed). No player input needed. (A unit that truly breaks free instead recovers cleanly -- see test/unit/test_morale_recovery_demo_scenario.gd for that case in isolation.)

Riders who stop riding while others of the troop still ride ride back to their places on a grid laid where the troop's riders were when every one of them rode (couple reads a troop off its men then), hundreds of wu off, and the shape is read off them (the chasers are left out, DemoChasers). A unit that falls in on its own men rather than on a laid grid is #1954. The spearmen (uid 1) read 20.71 on seed 0 and 0.00 on the rest (main 0.00): with the company cut down sooner, the squadrons turn on them, break at tick 988, and the spearmen follow the rout in their ranks, turning onto the routed squadron's centre while it stands clear of them (RoutedFront), which swings their grid: a facing read off what the men see is #1955.
